definition: A variant of the Adam optimizer that decouples weight decay from the gradient-based update, improving generalization.
details: AdamW is now the default optimizer for training most large transformer-based language models, replacing the L2-regularization approach used in the original Adam.
story: Think of a hiker descending a foggy hill in the dark, taking small steps and feeling for the steepest way down. The machine starts out clumsy, makes mistakes, and is nudged a little less wrong every time. It is the same loop you use to learn anything: try, miss, correct, try again. Skill, for a model, is just error pushed down until it is small enough to ignore. And that is AdamW — the quiet loop that turns flailing into skill.
